why: An ironmongery merchant whose content is good but whose access is shut. robots.txt disallows four answer crawlers and two training crawlers, and also disallows two real content paths; a WAF returns 403 to any AI user agent robots.txt does allow; one product page carries X-Robots-Tag noindex; the about page canonicalises to a different domain; the sitemap advertises a URL that 404s. This is the gate-1 fixture, and it also proves the answer-crawler versus training-crawler split.
note: This robots.txt blocks four AI crawlers by name. Two of them - GPTBot and ClaudeBot - are training crawlers by their operators' own documentation, so they belong with CCBot and Google-Extended in the info-severity rights decision, not in the citation defect. An earlier version of this audit put them in the answer group and told owners to allow-list them to be cited, which would have reopened the site to training collection it had deliberately opted out of. The answer-crawler block - OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot - must still be high.
